name: Attendance Allowance

clauses.text: Must have reached State Pension age.
Must have a physical or mental disability or health condition severe enough to need help with personal care or supervision.
Must have needed that help for at least 6 months.
Must have been in Great Britain for at least 2 of the last 3 years.
Cannot get Attendance Allowance if already receiving Disability Living Allowance, Personal Independence Payment, or Adult Disability Payment.
Paid at £76.70/week (lower rate) or £114.60/week (higher rate); higher rate when help needed both day and night.
Scheme covers England and Wales; people in Scotland apply for Pension Age Disability Payment.

questions.age_years: What is your date of birth? (used to calculate your age)
questions.state_pension_age: What is your date of birth? (used to determine your State Pension age)
questions.needs_care_help: Do you need help with personal care or supervision because of a disability or health condition?
questions.care_need_months: For how many months have you needed this help?
questions.in_gb_2_of_last_3_years: Have you been in Great Britain for at least 2 of the last 3 years?
questions.receives_dla_or_pip: Are you currently receiving Disability Living Allowance, Personal Independence Payment, or Adult Disability Payment?
questions.country: In which country do you live? (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland)

notes: Attendance Allowance is for people in England and Wales who have reached State Pension age and need care help. Higher rate paid if help needed both day and night.
